claims.claim: For distinct large primes with 3 coprime to p−1 and q−1, cubing is a permutation of all residues.
The modular inverse d can be chosen below phi(N)<N.
CRT proves (x³)^d=x also for nonunit x.
Decryption can use d without storing both factors.
claims.scope_note: Knowing d still enables factorization through m=3d−1.

claims.claim: For x³<N the ciphertext is the ordinary integer cube.
The logarithmic leading-block model gives probability approximately 1/3 below N^(1/3).
claims.scope_note: Model-dependent, not a universal distribution of messages.

claims.claim: Knowing an inverse algorithm is not shown equivalent to knowing factors.
claims.scope_note: Research exercise33 is not solved.

claims.claim: Knowing d supplies an exponent m=3d−1 for the factor reduction.
An m with a significant density of x^m=1 enables the exercise34 factor algorithm.
Three pairwise-coprime moduli reveal the integer cube when x is below each modulus.
claims.scope_note: Shared factors are exposed directly by gcd.

claims.claim: Seven known linear timestamp transformations yield the bounded cubic system of exercise44.
claims.scope_note: The power-of-two coefficient is a unit for odd RSA moduli; size assumptions retained.
Previously verified finite primality fact reused.

claims.claim: Binary powering uses 17 modular multiplications rather than 2, ratio8.5.
Any positive exponent coprime to phi(N) has a modular inverse on all residues.
Smooth p−1 and q−1 support the earlier order-based factor methods.
claims.scope_note: A proper-factor result still requires distinguishing the components.

claims.claim: The printed product bound fails when only one large prime factor is missing from m.
Close factors make Fermat factoring easier.
claims.scope_note: Reuse the exact Fermat search bound, not a uniform real-world timing claim.

claims.claim: A small rational approximation to p/q can help Lehman's variant.
claims.scope_note: Reuse the previously closed multiplier argument.

claims.claim: The proposed key construction is presented as a historical security assessment.
claims.scope_note: No unconditional unbreakability conclusion.

claims.claim: The first approximately90 odd-candidate estimate comes from a prime-density model.
claims.scope_note: Not a worst-case prime-gap theorem.

claims.claim: Fifty independent strong probable-prime trials have fixed-composite error at most2^−100.
claims.scope_note: This is not a posterior probability for every possible candidate source.

claims.claim: Even k with k≡p1 mod3 makes kp1+1 congruent to2 mod3.
The second approximately90-trial estimate uses the progression density.
claims.scope_note: Explicit heuristic, not a uniform finite-gap bound.

claims.claim: The construction has approximately120- and130-digit factors and a250-digit product.
claims.scope_note: Order-of-magnitude estimates with the stated ranges.

claims.claim: The earlier p+1 method motivates the additional smoothness check.
claims.scope_note: No claim of a complete security criterion.

claims.claim: 365.2425 days give31,556,952,000,000 microseconds per year.
10^25 microseconds are approximately3.1688·10^11 years.
claims.scope_note: Conditional illustration, not a measured factoring time.

claims.claim: The signed-directory discussion requires a trusted key and a suitable signature security model.
claims.scope_note: Generic unforgeability is not established here.

claims.claim: f=(p^(q−1)−q^(p−1)) mod N is−1 modulo p and+1 modulo q.
Unit squares have roots x,−x,fx,−fx.
claims.scope_note: Nonunit squares have fewer distinct roots; explicit minor qualification, no new card.

claims.claim: Parity or a half-interval selects two of the four unit roots.
A square-root oracle disagrees with±x with probability1/2 on a random unit square.
A nontrivial pair of square roots exposes p or q through gcd.
Access to a suitable square-root service permits the stated factor reduction.
claims.scope_note: The analogous general RSA reduction is not proved.

claims.claim: The unpadded branch admits x=floor(cuberoot(N)), whose cube is still below N.
claims.scope_note: C0167 persists after the known strict-upper-bound correction.

claims.claim: B=ceil(cuberoot(N)), J=floor(N/B), H=(J−B)B define a repaired scheme for N>=28.
Padded and unpadded representatives occupy disjoint ranges inside[B,N).
The threshold decoder and remainder modulo B recover the original message.
Every repaired representative is at least B and ciphertext cannot be an unreduced small cube.
The capacity loss is B²+(N mod B)=O(N^(2/3)).
claims.scope_note: Repairs the stated leakage only, not full encryption security.

claims.claim: The requested unrestricted reduction from RSA inversion to factoring is not obtained.
claims.scope_note: The archived2024 generic-model result does not solve the general exercise.

claims.claim: For uniform residues the root probabilities are P=gcd(m,p−1)/p and Q=gcd(m,q−1)/q.
Exactly one prime divides x^m−1 with probability P+Q−2PQ.
When one probability is at most1/2 and PQ>=10^−12, success is at least2(10^−6−10^−12).
This gives order10^6 log(m) modular operations in expectation.
If P,Q>1/2, m is a multiple of lcm(p−1,q−1).
The exact probability of equal two-adic component orders is at most1/2.
A differing two-adic order gives a nontrivial square root of one and a factor.
claims.scope_note: Use a gcd pretest for nonunits.

claims.claim: J(−x)=J(x)=−J(2x), including the zero-symbol case.
The candidates4x+2 and8x+4 fit0<z<N in the stated message range.
At least one candidate has Jacobi symbol>=0.
claims.scope_note: Apply the known2004 zero-symbol correction.

claims.claim: Among unit square roots there is one even root with positive Jacobi symbol.
A nonzero nonunit square has two opposite roots and exactly one even root.
The mod4 branch and floor by4 or8 recover x.
An input with negative Jacobi symbol forces a different root class and reveals a factor.
If only the decoded message is returned, three possible representatives suffice to find the returned root.
More than half of unit squares are valid ciphertexts, preserving the factor reduction under that promise.
The stated lattice short-vector guarantee is the supplied algorithmic input.
claims.scope_note: LLL is an explicitly named external theorem, not independently reproved in this block.

claims.claim: The answer treats degree<d with k=d(d−1)/2+1 congruences.
The coefficients u_i isolate each modulus.
The triangular block matrix encodes the congruences and has nonzero determinant.
Scaling L by d clears denominators without changing the short-vector comparison.
The stated lower bound on m implies length(vL)<M/d.
For d=4,n=11, the exact threshold is below10^27.
claims.scope_note: Reuse the saved integer-square-root comparison.

claims.claim: The short vector defines a polynomial P with P(x) divisible by every m_i.
The coefficient length bounds and |x|<m give |P(x)|<M, hence P(x)=0.
The collective gcd assumption and the last coordinates prevent P from vanishing identically.
The nonzero polynomial has at most d−1 candidate roots.
Bounded integer roots can be isolated and checked in polynomial time for fixed d.
claims.scope_note: Sturm's theorem is an explicit input; the dyadic interval algorithm is given.
